items.title: Susinsight
items.subtitle: Editorial & Analysis Platform
items.short: Independent reporting and analysis on sustainability and development, with a particular depth in African contexts.
items.content:
What Susinsight Is

Susinsight is where research meets storytelling. It's an editorial platform covering sustainability and development across Africa, written for policy makers, business leaders, researchers, professionals, and citizens who need depth, not just headlines.

The work connects systems to human realities: what's changing, why it matters, and what decisions are being shaped by those changes. Every piece is grounded in evidence, shaped by context, and published to advance understanding.

What We Publish

  • Deep Analysis: In-depth reports on economic, environmental, and social forces shaping African development.
  • Explainers: Clear breakdowns of complex issues, no jargon, no assumptions, just usable clarity.
  • Narratives: Stories that connect policy to practice, showing what change looks like on the ground.
  • Intelligence Briefs: Research-backed insights for leaders, practitioners, and citizens navigating sustainability challenges.

Why It Exists

Publishing keeps thinking honest. Ideas that sit only in reports or strategy decks don't get tested. Susinsight creates space to explore questions openly, refine frameworks through public scrutiny, and contribute to conversations shaping Africa's future.

It's not content for content's sake. It's a commitment to building knowledge in public, where others can use it, challenge it, and build on it.

Visit Susinsight →

items.title: Susdata
items.subtitle: Data & Measurement Initiative
items.short: Indicators, analytics, and visual tools that make sustainability and development data usable.
items.content:
What Susdata Is

Susdata is where data becomes insight. It's a platform for building indicators, tools, and visualizations that help organizations move from raw numbers to practical understanding.

Most sustainability data exists in formats designed for reporting, not decision-making. Susdata closes that gap, turning datasets into dashboards, metrics into meaning, and complexity into clarity.

What We Build

  • Indicators: Sustainability and development metrics designed to reveal progress, risk, and opportunity across African economies and sectors.
  • Analytics Tools: Dashboards and calculators that make it easier to see patterns, track change, and surface what matters.
  • Visual Systems: Data storytelling and visualization that connect numbers to narratives, making evidence accessible and actionable.

Why It Exists

Data only works when people can use it. Susdata exists to close the distance between measurement and action, building systems that translate technical indicators into tools teams can actually apply.

Every dataset is a starting point. The real work is making it legible, trustworthy, and useful where decisions get made.

Explore Susdata →

items.title: Knowledge Lab
items.subtitle: Research & Experimentation Space
items.short: A space for pilots, applied research, and new methods for communicating impact.
items.content:
What the Knowledge Lab Is

Knowledge Lab is where we test ideas before they become methods. It's a space for piloting approaches, exploring new formats for impact communication, and running applied research projects that push beyond standard practice.

Not everything here succeeds, and that's the point. The lab creates room to experiment, fail forward, and develop sharper tools for making sustainability knowledge work in real contexts.

What We Work On

  • Methodological Experiments: Testing new frameworks for lifecycle assessment, impact measurement, and evidence synthesis.
  • Communication Pilots: Exploring formats, platforms, and narratives that help complex information land with the people who need to act on it.
  • Applied Research: Small-scale studies that ask practical questions: What works? What doesn't? What's missing?

Why It Exists

The lab exists because consulting shouldn't only draw from what's already proven. It should help develop what's next.

By working in public, publishing findings, sharing methods, and inviting scrutiny, we stay connected to emerging questions, sharpen our thinking, and contribute to the broader field of sustainability practice.
